I need to ask about the nature of his feeding difficulties; is he choking or regurgitating large amounts of milk after feeds? Also, has he been passing gas or stool normally?

Please describe any specific behaviors you notice during feeding and his bowel habits.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon). The clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with progressive abdominal distension, vomiting, and pain on palpation is highly suggestive of intestinal obstruction due to the lack of ganglion cells. Immediate evaluation with a rectal exam and contrast enema is required to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like intestinal atresia or volvulus.
